items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to contracts for the transportation of school children
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5984

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
contracts for the transportation of school children

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  To restore employee protection
provisions to school bus contracts in NYC

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:  Statement of legislative findings regarding
employee protection provisions, and pension liability. This bill
amends section 305 of the education law to restore employee protection
provisions (EPPs) in school bus contracts in NYC.

JUSTIFICATION:  EPPs create a master seniority list that school bus
companies must use to fill job vacancies. The master seniority list is
comprised of employees who become unemployed as a result. of
reassignment of busing contracts. EPPs require bus contractors to give
priority, by seniority, to veteran drivers at the same pay and
benefits, including pension rate, as their most recent jobs.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:  To be determined

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law and the tax law, in relation to contracts for the transportation of school children
A.lawCode: Amd §305, Ed L; amd §1115, Tax L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5984A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law and the tax law, in relation to
contracts for the transportation of school children

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To restore employee protection provisions to school bus contracts in
NYC, to allow for the use of the employment cost index for the
calculation of the extension of school bus contracts and to exempt
school bus purchases from sales tax

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of this bill contains legislative findings

Section two of this bill amends paragraph a of subdivision 14 of
section 305 of the Education Law to require the New York City
Department of Education (NYC DOE) to include in its solicitations for
contracts for school bus transportation for children in grades
kindergarten through 12 ("school bus contracts") provisions for the
retention or preference in hiring and the preservation of wages,
health, welfare and retirement benefits and seniority of employees who
perform or performed work for employers party to such contracts, in
connection with such contracts and change the index used as a
negotiation cap for the extension of school transportation contracts
throughout the state from the Consumer Price Index (CPI) to the
Employment Cost Index (ECI).

Section three amends paragraph c of subdivision 14 of section 305 of
the education law by amending the reference to the Consumer Price
Index (CPI) to the Employment Cost Index (ECI).

Section four amends subdivision 14 of section 305 of the Education Law
by adding a new paragraph g, which would authorize NYC DOE to seek to
amend school bus contracts to include provisions for the retention or
preference in hiring and the preservation of wages, health, welfare
and retirement benefits and seniority of employees who perform or
performed work for employers party to such contracts, in connection
with such contracts.

Section five amends subdivision a of section 1115 of the tax law by
adding a new paragraph 44 to exempt school buses, parts, equipment,
lubricants and fuel from New York State sales tax.

Section six would include a severability clause.

Section seven is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This package of proposals for the school bus industry are needed to
bring stability and certainty to the industry.

The EPPs create a master seniority list that school bus companies must
use to fill job vacancies. The master seniority list is comprised of
employees who become unemployed as a result of reassignment of busing
contracts. EPPs require bus contractors to give priority, by
seniority, to veteran drivers at the same pay and benefits, including
pension rate, as their most recent jobs.

The EPP proposal will ensure that NYC DOE's future school bus
contracts will include provisions designed to avoid service disruption
and pension withdrawal liability claims, while protecting the
experienced school bus contract workforce from drastic wage and
benefit reductions and facilitating the retention of an experienced
workforce. It will also enable NYC DOE to seek to amend existing
contracts that do not include such provisions to include them.

The change in the index that is used as a negotiation cap for the
extension of school transportation contracts throughout the state is
needed to better reflect the changes in the industry. Current contract
extensions are governed by the Consumer Price Index for Urban areas
(CPI-U). This index is an economic indicator of peoples buying habits
associated with apparel, housing, food and recreation - items not
associated with school transportation contracts. This proposal calls
for using the Employment Cost Index (ECI) instead of the CPI-U. The
ECI is a reflection of labor cost and is a more accurate index to
govern the costs of transportation contracts given that 65-70 percent
of the costs come from labor contracts. The CPI-U can vary greatly,
with extreme highs and lows; whereas the ECI is a more stable number
without the drastic highs and lows and works out to about the same
percentage increase as a 10-year average of the CPI-U. Again, this is
a negotiation cap - the school district retains sole discretion and
may keep increases to zero.

Finally, this proposal would exempt school buses and associated items
(parts, equipment, lubricants and fuel) from state and local sales
tax. School buses are the only buses not currently exempt from sales
tax. Exempting them from sales tax would allow the contractors to
convey the savings realized from not paying the tax to the school
district as part of the contract negotiations and/or request for
proposal process.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that the
provisions of section 5 shall take effect on the first day of a
quarterly sales tax period, as set forth in subdivision (b) of section
1136 of the tax law, next succeeding April 1, 2017
